Each Game has an explicit ExecutionRole : Client , IntegratedServer or DedicatedServer , selected before construction in Options.execution_role . Startup, world loading and opening other dimensions use that role. Only clients mesh chunks and show loading progress; a client can still run its simulation in-frame, which is deprecated and will be removed. Connecting

It should be one small native program with no Java and no Python, one command to install it, one config file, and a CLI, a web panel and a control API to manage it. At the same view and simulation distance and with the same players, it should beat vanilla, Paper and Fabric + Lithium on TPS/MSPT, RAM, CPU, chunk generation and start time. Player names. usercache.json in the universe folder works as vanilla's CachedUserNameToIdResolver . Players are added when they join and kept for a month, and the file keeps the 1000 most recently used, newest first. The console finds a player by name in it, in any case. x: Survival multiplayer (SMP): the official server's mod The official Rusty Minecraft server (horizon.bunchy7s.dev) wants an organised survival game: a currency players earn in game, a server market, safe player-to-player trades, small games of chance with that currency, and spawn, homes, teleport requests, warps, land claims and rules. Structure terrain-adaptation density horizon_core::density::Beardifier implements the pinned Java Edition 26.3 structure-density sampler from supplied ordered rigid pieces, jigsaw junctions and an affected bounding box. It supports NONE , BURY , BEARD_THIN , BEARD_BOX and ENCAPSULATE adjustments. Live structure discovery, filtering and placement remain separate work. The sampler retains float accumulation order, wrapped coordinate arithmetic, ground-level deltas, the 24-by-24-by-24 kernel and vanilla's inverse-square-root approximation. Its kernel is computed once from the formula. No extracted vanilla kernel data is stored in the source tree. The immutable sampler can be attached to WorldField::Beardifier and shared between worker contexts. Scalar reads return zero outside the affected box. Bulk reads clear the entire output, including an oversized tail, then scan the clipped strided volume. Vanilla floors the lower clipping index rather than rounding it upward, so a first bulk sample can be outside the scalar bounds. Rusty Minecraft preserves this scalar/bulk distinction. A missing affected box produces zero even if component lists are nonempty. Bounds supplied to the Rust constructor must already be normalized; short output buffers return a typed error before mutation. Run: python3 tools/test_structure_density_parity.py The local report records 1,360,095 matching output lines per reference JAR across 183 fixtures , 28,093 scalar queries and 339 volumes . The original Java adapter calls the actual Beardifier constructor and samplers. Cases include every adjustment mode, the full junction kernel neighborhood, ground offsets, overlapping components, reversed accumulation order, null/empty bounds, floor clipping, output tails and extreme wrapped coordinates. Float outputs are compared by raw bits with canonical NaNs. The report records the authenticated JARs, source and fixture hashes. Raw outputs stay private under .local . CI runs the comparison on its configured platforms; the local Math.pow -derived kernel check does not establish cross-platform math parity. The noise-fill comparison also checks supplied structure density through final-density and aquifer graphs. Structure-start selection, invalid-box repair and complete structure terrain generation remain pending.

x: World height: each level's shape from its dimension type Vanilla takes each level's build range from its dimension type: min_y and height , multiples of 16, with height >= 16 and min_y + height <= 2032 ( DimensionType.MIN_Y = -2032 , Y_SIZE = 4064 : BlockPos packs Y in 12 bits), plus logical_height (how high portals and chorus fruit reach) and has_skylight . LevelHeightAccessor derives everything else from them. Data packs that reshape the Overworld make it taller: JJThunder's To The Max sets min_y -64, height 2096 , the largest top vanilla allows, which is 131 sections against vanilla's 24. The model chunk::LevelShape is one level's shape: min_y , height , logical_height , sky_light , checked as the dimension type codec checks them ( LevelShape::new ). LevelShapes holds a world's three. Where it comes from. A local world's shapes are its dimension types, its enabled data packs' over vanilla's, through the level stems that name them ( worldgen::overrides::WorldgenOverrides::level_height , read by game/world_loading.rs 's level_shapes when the world opens; the game keeps them in Game.level_shapes ). A remote client takes a level's shape from the server's minecraft:dimension_type registry ( protocol::registry::DimensionType , with its logical height). A type the codec refuses keeps the vanilla shape, with a warning. Where it lives. Each level's World holds its shape , SaveDir::new(root, shape) takes it, and the generator reads the same dimension type for the level's build range ( OverworldGenerator::level ). The column. LevelShape::column() is the span of sections the level's chunks hold ( ColumnLayout ): the level's own range, widened to the vanilla Overworld's -64..320 . So vanilla's three levels keep the 24 sections they have always had, and a taller Overworld gets its own column while its Nether and End stay at 24. Every Chunk records its own min_y and section count, and the hot accessors read the chunk. No global.
